title: Combined Side-Channel and DFA Attack on DEFAULT
summary: It remains open how far an attack combining side-channel analysis with differential fault analysis can be carried against the DEFAULT cipher.

formal_statement.body: Determine how far a combined side-channel analysis and differential fault analysis (DFA) attack can be carried against the DEFAULT cipher. Because the question fixes no side-channel leakage model, fault model, ordering or interaction of attack stages, or success metric, a resolution should state these choices, construct and evaluate the combined attack, and characterize its resulting capability against DEFAULT.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key cryptanalysis of the DEFAULT cipher using combined side-channel analysis and differential fault analysis.
parameters: Side-channel leakage model — defines the leakage observations available to the attack
Fault model — defines the faulty executions or outputs available to the attack
Attack-stage ordering or interaction — determines how side-channel and differential-fault information are combined
Success metric — measures the resulting attack capability
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct and evaluate a combined side-channel and DFA attack under stated choices and characterize its capability against DEFAULT.

citations.label: DEFAULT: Cipher Level Resistance Against Differential Fault Attack

progress.summary: The source presents this as a future attack direction, asking how far combined side-channel analysis and DFA can go against DEFAULT. It leaves the attack models, their interaction, and the success metric open.
citation_labels: Anubhab Baksi et al., DEFAULT: Cipher Level Resistance Against Differential Fault Attack
